brief: Fed communication remains hawkish into December, with debate centered on hike size. Waller still pushes a 50bp hike and wants last year's three insurance cuts reversed, while Musalem, Logan and Hammack back smaller increments and Williams sees no need for dramatic action. Natixis doubts 50bp happens but expects a hawkish December meeting that keeps January well priced. October retail sales and the control group beat expectations despite auto and furniture softness, reinforcing the resilience the Fed will weigh alongside next week's PCE, forecast to hold near 3.8% and 3.2% y/y headline and core. With equities now the main driver of rates, Natixis stays on the sidelines, favoring long-end dips only above 5.20%-5.25%, inside a 4.90%-5.25% range for 10s into the December meeting. On swap spreads, AI-related loan hedging, about $320mm/01, has kept 10yr spreads roughly 12bps wide. As that buildout activity is expected to ease in 1Q27, Natixis scales into long spreads at -42.5bps and -45bps, targeting -35bps. Separately, Brazil's fiscal risks are weighing on the BRL, and Chile's Q3 GDP contraction has not changed Natixis's call for an unchanged 4.50% policy rate.
